books.title: All the Sinners Bleed
books.author: S. A. Cosby

books.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie

books.author: Jacqueline Woodson

books.title: Another Country
books.author: James Baldwin

books.title: Anybody's Daughter
books.author: Pamela Samuels Young

A teenage girl is lured away by someone she met online.
Her uncle Dre, who has a criminal past, searches for her with help from attorney Angela Evans.

books.title: The Autobiography of an Ex-Colored Man
books.author: James Weldon Johnson
books.blurb: First published anonymously in 1912, this novel is told by an unnamed, light-skinned musician who moves through Black and white America and Europe. After witnessing a lynching, he chooses to pass as white, and wonders what he has given up.

books.author: Ernest J. Gaines
books.blurb: Despite its title, this is a novel: the fictional life story of a woman who is over 100 years old, told to a history teacher. Born enslaved in Louisiana, Jane lives from the Civil War to the civil rights movement of the 1960s.

books.title: The Awkward Black Man
books.author: Walter Mosley
books.blurb: In seventeen stories, Walter Mosley turns away from tough-guy heroes to write about Black men who are nerdy, self-defeating, or just odd: a lonely man facing illness, an overqualified mailroom clerk whose only companion is a fly, a struggling drinker who finds surprising success as a Zen-like panhandler.

books.title: Behold the Dreamers
books.author: Imbolo Mbue
books.blurb: Jende Jonga, an immigrant from Cameroon living in Harlem, lands a job as chauffeur for a Lehman Brothers executive, while his wife Neni dreams of becoming a pharmacist. Then the 2008 financial crisis hits, and both families, rich and poor, see their American dreams crack apart.

An immigrant from Cameroon becomes a driver for a Wall Street executive.

books.title: Beloved
books.author: Toni Morrison
books.blurb: After escaping slavery in Kentucky, Sethe lives in a house outside Cincinnati haunted by the ghost of her baby daughter. books.title: The Best of Simple
books.author: Langston Hughes
books.blurb: A collection of humorous sketches featuring Jesse B. Semple, a Harlem everyman who talks about race, women, work, and life over drinks with a more educated friend. The pieces first ran as newspaper columns.

books.author: Walter Mosley
books.blurb: In 1961 Los Angeles, Easy Rawlins is hired to find Elizabeth Eady, a beautiful woman he knew in Houston who has vanished from her job as a housekeeper for a wealthy Beverly Hills family. Meanwhile, his friend Mouse is out of prison and looking for revenge.

A detective searches for a missing housekeeper from his past.

books.title: Black Candle Women
books.author: Diane Marie Brown
books.blurb: Four generations of Montrose women share a California bungalow and a collection of spells and tinctures. When seventeen-year-old Nickie brings home her first boyfriend, the family's hidden secret surfaces: a decades-old curse that kills anyone they fall in love with. books.title: The Bluest Eye
books.author: Toni Morrison
books.blurb: In 1941 Lorain, Ohio, eleven-year-old Pecola Breedlove prays every night for blue eyes, believing they would make her beautiful and loved. Narrated partly by her classmate Claudia, the novel traces how racism, colorism, and family trauma destroy a child.

books.title: The Book of Harlan
books.author: Bernice L. McFadden
books.blurb: Born in Macon, Georgia, in 1917, Harlan moves with his family to Harlem and becomes a musician. He and his trumpeter friend Lizard Robbins travel to Paris to play the Montmartre cabaret scene, but when the Nazis occupy the city both are sent to the Buchenwald concentration camp, an experience that changes Harlan forever.

Two Black American jazz musicians are caught in Nazi-occupied France.

books.author: Lawrence Hill
books.blurb: Kidnapped from West Africa at eleven, Aminata Diallo survives the Middle Passage and enslavement in South Carolina. Her journey takes her through the American Revolution, to Nova Scotia with Black Loyalists, Sierra Leone, and finally London, where she tells her story to abolitionists.

books.author: Marlon James

books.author: Clay Cane

Characters including Luke, Henri, Josephine, and Charity Butler each fight back in their own way.

books.title: Cane
books.author: Jean Toomer
books.blurb: An experimental 1923 work that blends short stories, poems, and a play into a portrait of Black life in rural Georgia and in the cities of the North. It's considered a cornerstone of the Harlem Renaissance.

books.author: Lalita Tademy
books.blurb: Based on the author's own family, this saga follows four generations of women, Elisabeth, Suzette, Philomene, and Emily, along Louisiana's Cane River, from slavery through freedom, as each fights to keep her family together.

books.author: Nana Kwame Adjei-Brenyah

Loretta Thurwar is weeks away from earning release, and her partner Hurricane Staxxx is a fan favorite. It imagines a near-future United States.
Incarcerated people fight gladiator-style on TV for a chance at freedom.

books.title: The Changeling
books.author: Victor LaValle
books.blurb: Apollo Kagwa, a used-book dealer in New York, becomes a devoted new father, until his wife Emma commits a shocking act and vanishes. A new father deals in rare and used books.
Apollo Kagwa searches for his wife Emma after she does something terrible to their baby.

books.title: The Coldest Winter Ever
books.author: Sister Souljah
books.blurb: Winter Santiaga, the spoiled daughter of a Brooklyn drug kingpin, loses everything when her father is arrested. Determined to keep her lifestyle, she schemes and hustles through group homes and the streets, refusing to learn from her mistakes.

A kingpin's spoiled daughter loses everything after her father's arrest.
The heroine shares her name with the coldest season.

books.title: The Color Purple
books.author: Alice Walker

Celie finds strength through Shug Avery and letters from her sister Nettie.

books.author: Danzy Senna
books.blurb: Jane, a mixed-race novelist, has spent a decade on her 'masterpiece' about mixed-race history, while house-sitting in the Los Angeles hills with her painter husband and their kids. clues: This is a 2024 satirical novel about art and ambition.

A mixed-race novelist abandons her long-labored book to try writing for TV.

books.author: Delores Phillips

It's set in rural Georgia in 1958.
A mother abuses her many children.
Tangy Mae dreams of escaping her mother, Rosie.

books.title: Deacon King Kong
books.author: James McBride

In the aftermath, the whole community, from churchwomen to cops to mobsters, gets pulled in, in a big-hearted, comic portrait of a neighborhood.

An old church elder shoots a young drug dealer in broad daylight.

books.author: Nnedi Okorafor
books.blurb: Zelu, a disabled Nigerian American writer, has always felt like the outsider in her big Nigerian family. When it makes her a literary star, she starts to lose control of her own story.

The heroine uses a wheelchair and writes fiction against her family's wishes.

books.author: Sister Souljah
books.blurb: Porsche Santiaga, the fierce younger sister of Winter, refuses to accept her family's fall from Brooklyn hustler royalty. The narrator is the younger sister of the earlier book's heroine.
Porsche Santiaga, Winter's sister, fights her way out of juvenile detention.

books.author: Walter Mosley
books.blurb: In 1948 Los Angeles, WWII veteran Easy Rawlins has just lost his job when a white man pays him to find Daphne Monet, a mysterious white woman known to hang out in Black jazz clubs. The search pulls Easy into murder, politics, and his first case as a detective.

A laid-off veteran is hired to find a missing woman.

books.title: Didn't Nobody Give a Shit What Happened to Carlotta
books.author: James Hannaham
books.blurb: Carlotta Mercedes, a trans woman who spent more than twenty years in a men's prison after a robbery went wrong, is granted conditional release. Its heroine is a trans woman just released on parole after decades in a men's prison.
Released after more than 20 years, she tries to reunite with her son without violating parole.

books.title: Dominion
books.author: Addie E. Citchens

His favorite son, a football star called Wonderboy, can do no wrong in the community's eyes, until his violence can no longer be ignored. Told by the reverend's wife Priscilla and Diamond, the young woman who loves Wonderboy.

A powerful preacher and his community protect his golden-boy son.

books.author: Jewell Parker Rhodes

books.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie

clues: This 2025 novel was its author's first novel in over a decade.
It follows four women in Nigeria and America.

The women are Chiamaka, Zikora, Omelogor, and Kadiatou.

books.author: Percival Everett

clues: This satirical novel inspired the Oscar-winning 2023 film 'American Fiction'.
Its hero is a frustrated, highly literary writer and professor.
He writes a stereotype-filled parody under a fake name, and it becomes a hit.

books.title: Fences
books.author: August Wilson

A former Negro Leagues player now works as a garbage collector.

A violent incident at a 1971 concert ends in a death.
Journalist Sunny Shelton interviews everyone about a Detroit punk singer and her British partner.

books.author: Ntozake Shange

A college student goes south to help with voter registration.

An American man waits for his fiancée while torn by another relationship.

The heroine works in the cosmetics industry and goes by a one-word name.
